newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Procedure for deciding who qualifies for EMU.
newsitem.headline: Procedure for deciding who qualifies for EMU.

text.p: European Union countries will decide which among them will their planned monetary union (EMU) in early 1998.
The following is the procedure as laid out in the Maastrict Treaty:

-- The European Commission and the European Monetary Institute will report to the ECOFIN, the council of economy and finance ministers, on how each member state fared in meeting the EMU criteria in 1997.
-- The ECOFIN will vote on each county, using the EU's qualified majority voting procedure. The result will be sent to a summit of EU leaders for a final -- consensus -- decision.
-- Under qualified majority voting, each country has a weighted vote, loosely related to its size.
-- There are 87 votes in total. Sixty-two votes are needed for a qualified majority, meaning that if a group of countries can come up with 26 votes, they can reject or block the report.

-- Germany, Britain, France and Italy each have 10 votes. Spain has eight. The Netherlands, Greece, Belgium and Portugal have five. Sweden and Austria have four. Denmark, Finland and Ireland have three. Luxembourg has two.
-- The breakdown means - in theory - that the "Club Med" countries of Italy, Spain, Portugal and Greece could stop EMU if they believed they were being unfairly left out.
-- Conversely, a "hard core" group of Germany, Belgium, the Netherlands, Austria and Luxembourg could stop EMU if they though countries that did not deserve to qualify were about to be let in.
